leverage.exposure: The balance is positive right now and there is no open leveraged position, so nothing is at risk as things stand. The recommended move deliberately opens one: winning Mokwa takes the balance negative until Conté is sold, and a negative balance when the matchday starts scores zero for the entire matchday. The timing is comfortable rather than tight — the auction resolves roughly a day and a half before the lock, leaving a wide margin to complete the sale — but the sequence is not optional, and the leg that closes it is a manual sale only Georg can make. The failure mode to watch is the auction resolving overnight while unattended and the sale not following: that, and not the price paid, is the thing that would cost a whole matchday. If the auction is lost instead, the correct response is to do nothing at all, because the sale that would follow it must not happen on its own.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is the eleven-man floor, not the board and not the budget. With exactly eleven bodies and one legal shape, no sale can happen before a purchase lands, which is why every sale in this briefing is conditional on a buy clearing first and why the order of operations matters more than the prices. The second constraint behind it is the unwind ceiling: each purchase permits exactly one sale, so the most Georg can spend is bounded by the single largest body he is actually willing to lose, valued at the lock. That pair of constraints, not affordability, is what kills the expensive defenders and midfielders on the board. Spending power looks ample and is largely unusable.

verdict.headline: No new trade this run.
verdict.detail: No new trade this run. The position is unchanged and correct: the standing instruction from 16:45Z still stands, and it is still unexecuted. Raise the live Mokwa offer to 9.500.000 before the auction resolves overnight, then sell Conté the moment Mokwa lands. Nothing else on the board earns a place, and the squad is fit end to end. The real work this run was in the ledger, not the market: the open-call backlog had grown to the point where the two calls that ARE the live position were invisible to the run meant to reconcile them.

sell.reason: Conté remains the sale, conditionally and only after Mokwa lands. The ground is rank, not fitness, and this run confirms it twice over: he is fit, and Hoffenheim's own projected side has him in it for the Stuttgart game. Being fit and being projected does not rescue him — his season usage is mostly from the bench, his most recent matchday was negative, and he is comfortably the weakest scoring slot in the fielded eleven. He is also the only body whose proceeds cover the Mokwa bid while leaving a legal shape behind. The condition is absolute and unchanged: if the Mokwa auction is LOST, the sale must NOT happen, because the squad is at exactly eleven and selling him drops it to ten for the under-eleven penalty. No other sale is recommended, and no other sale is even possible without a body arriving first.

buy.reason: Mokwa, and nothing else. The objection that once blocked him is now dead from both directions: he is fit, not in his club's absence list, and the projected Elversberg attack that previously omitted him now includes him. He started both matchdays and scored in them, and he is worth a large points gain over the slot he would take. The instruction is to raise, not to sit: the current standing bid sits below every contested clearing this ledger has measured, and the one time we bid at that kind of level on a contested listing we lost the player to a much larger premium. The raise target stays where the last run set it, at the top of the measured band and still inside the ceiling that keeps the balance clearing before the lock. Two players that would otherwise headline a buy list are refused on fresh dated evidence rather than on price alone. Pavlović has the best scoring average on the board and his club's own projected midfield does not include him, so he is a rotation risk at a very large price. Castello Lukeba is the more interesting case and the closer call: the fitness flag that rejected him days ago is gone, and the freshest source in this entire sweep has him starting. He is logged as a watch with explicit entry conditions rather than a buy, because the only sale big enough to fund him would force a formation this ledger has never confirmed is legal, and because his scoring average rests on a single match played either side of a muscle injury. His seller's asking price has sat unsold for days, so if he is ever taken, he is taken near value and never at the ask.

standing.name: David Mokwa
standing.why: RAISE THE LIVE OFFER FROM 8.300.000 TO 9.500.000, AND THIS RUN FORMALLY CLOSES AVOID Ar95t3l WHOSE STRICT REVERSAL CONDITION IS STILL UNMET - said plainly because it is a reversal. Ar95t3l required "an Elversberg XI dated 09.09.2026 or later that actually starts him". No such XI exists: ligainsider's Elversberg page is STILL timestamped 07.09.2026 18:51, unchanged since Ar95t3l read it, and still omits him. I am overriding that condition on one specific ground, not on impatience: the source that generates the condition contradicts itself. THE SELF-CONTRADICTION, IN FIGURES. Ligainsider's own Mokwa player page reports 2 Bundesliga starts out of 2 matchdays, 195 league minutes, 2 goals, 0 assists, and no injury item newer than preseason (Erkaeltung 15.08.2026, angeschlagen 27.07.2026, "bereit" 20.08.2026 - all stale by the date-trap rule). Kickbase agrees independently: st 0, smc 2, ismc 2, smdc 2, ph hp TRUE for both matchdays at 150 and 148, tp 298, ap 149, g 2, sec 9981. He is not in Elversberg's verletzt/gesperrt table (only Seifert and Zimmerschied are). Meanwhile the same probable-XI graphic that benches a 2-of-2 starter with 2 goals STARTS Luca Sirch, who has ap 18 on 35 points and whom this ledger already caught the graphic mis-listing. A projection that inverts its own club's usage data on two players at once is a broken instrument, not dated selection evidence. Ar95t3l itself recorded the honest case for reversing (fit, not injured, 84% of minutes, "a rotation forward omitted from one projection, not a benching") and declined only because the condition was literal. This run judges the condition unmeetable-by-construction while that page stays frozen, and MD3 kicks off 2026-09-13T15:30Z. WHY RAISE RATHER THAN HOLD AT 8.300.000. 8.300.000 over mv 6.847.645 is +21,21%, the very top of the old +17-21% band - but this run measured a NEW contested board clear that beats it: Hansen to Borussia Rumpelfuss at 14:15:02Z, 7.300.000 against mv 5.944.803 = +22,80%. Our own calibration table is two losses deep from exactly this error: Banks bid +15,01% cleared +30,43%, Makengo bid +13,03% cleared +60,76%, both lost on the advice to hold. 9.500.000 = +38,73% clears every measured board clear in this league except the Makengo outlier. THE COST IS ZERO IN POINTS TERMS: the unwind self-funds. 333.904 - 9.500.000 = -9.166.096, then Conte at mv 10.096.062 (mvt 1 rising, sdmvt +1.454.448, and tonight's 20:00Z update should lift it further) returns +929.966, eleven bodies, 4-3-3 legal. Ceiling before the balance breaks is about 10.430.000, so 9.500.000 keeps a real margin. POINTS: Mokwa ap 149 replaces Conte ap 47 in the fielded eleven, +102, XI ap 1342 to 1444, at 46k per point against Conte's 215k. Listing is a Kickbase board listing at exactly mv, ofc 1 with only Georg in ofs - uncontested as a snapshot, which after Makengo is explicitly NOT a forecast.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. Every manager ask currently on the board sits above market value, so the mechanism a flip depends on is simply absent — there is nothing to buy below value and drift upward. Rivals continue to churn players in and out within minutes for fractions of a percent, including one round trip completed inside thirteen minutes this evening on a player who returned almost exactly what he cost. That is motion, not points, and it is not a model to copy. The flip window is technically still open on time, but there is nothing in it.

fitness.sweep: A clean sweep, which is the headline: not one of the eleven carries a current dated injury, suspension or doubt, and the two clubs whose projected sides matter most for the recommended trade both name our players in them. The only exit item anywhere in the squad is the Fulham interest in Matsima, and that is settled rather than live — his club publicly refused the approach, his contract runs for years, and the window is shut, so it is a January question at the earliest and needs no action now. Two stale-date traps were caught and discarded during the sweep, including an injury flag on one of our midfielders whose only dated news is from July and whose club's projected side, updated this evening, has him starting. Both players in the recommended trade were verified against sources dated within the last two days, and the buy target was additionally checked for any newer source that would rule him out. None exists.
